newsitem.title: UK: Colombia's Harf calls for 14 pct peso devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Harf calls for 14 pct peso devaluation.

text.p: Colombia's foreign trade minister said on Monday he would like to see the peso devalued by 14 percent between now and June next year.
"The devaluation should be increased to achieve 14 percent between now and June 1997," Morris Harf Meyer told Reuters in an interview in London.
Until August this year Colombia's accumulated devaluation has been less than 6.0 percent, he said.
Colombia had envisaged a 14 percent devaluation of the peso for the full year but so far the currency has slipped less than half that amount, prompting his call for a speedier fall.
Colombia's exporters have been pressing increasingly for the peso to be devalued and Harf said he fully supported these moves.
"We are trying to co-ordinate with the central bank to maintain the exchange rate equilibrium so our exports don't lose competitiveness," he said.

"It is unfair that Colombian businessmen who have worked hard to gain entry into international markets should lose that because of an artificial revaluation of the Colombian peso," he said. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
